summary: S5 is substantially implemented and all five reported gates pass, but the batch is not ready: the S3 policy breaks the required upload contract, production can inherit an unapproved seven-day PHI retention policy, and required live recovery/security acceptance evidence remains pending. The planning guide is ignored and absent from HEAD, so its modification history cannot be verified against the requested baseline.
substeps_covered: Prerequisites — complete for authored infrastructure: S4 supplies private database placement, security groups, and the S3 gateway endpoint; S0 supplies synthetic-staging defaults. Production retention policy remains unresolved.

S5.1 RDS — partial: private encrypted PostgreSQL 16, db.t4g.small, 50 GiB gp3, capped autoscaling, scheduled maintenance/backups, deletion protection, and final snapshots are configured. Regional availability and a supported minor remain unverified.
S5.2 recovery — partial: staging has seven-day backups and production requires an explicit backup decision, but no backup or LatestRestorableTime has been observed.
S5.3 database TLS — complete in configuration: rds.force_ssl=1 and existing client verify-full CA/hostname checks agree.
S5.4 audio storage — incorrect: public-access blocks, owner-enforced ownership, versioning, SSE-KMS, Bucket Keys, and TLS policies exist, but headerless presigned PUTs are denied.
S5.5 lifecycle — complete for synthetic staging; production current/noncurrent retention is incorrectly allowed to default to seven days.
S5.6 overwrite race — complete as an explicit Step 9 deferral; documentation correctly prohibits immutability claims.

S5.7 queues — complete in default configuration: standard queue and DLQ, 300-second visibility, 20-second polling, three receives, 4/14-day retention, source-restricted redrive, SSE-KMS, and insecure-transport denial.
S5.8 key boundaries and retained copies — complete in design: application data has a distinct rotating KMS key and documentation identifies unrecoverability and duplicate-copy risks.
S5.9 exports — complete: no unsupported export bucket was introduced.

Later-step integration — compatible at interface level: manifests expose bucket, queue, database, and key identifiers while leaving IAM grants and runtime credentials to S6 and restore/version binding to Step 9.

HIPAA-focused review — no authentication, session, application authorization, tenant-isolation, or audit-event code changed. The confirmed retention risk is listed below; runtime least-privilege enforcement remains pending S6 and no compliance conclusion follows from the passing tests.
Validation — fmt, clippy, test, tf-manifest, and tf-network passed as reported. Mock tests validate Terraform structure but do not establish live AWS behavior.

blockers.problem: Confirmed availability defect: the PutObject deny statements use StringNotEqualsIfExists. With an explicit Deny, the negated IfExists condition also matches when the header is absent. The application presigner sends Content-Type but no SSE headers (crates/er-server/src/routes.rs:284), so normal uploads are rejected instead of receiving bucket-default SSE-KMS. The structural test at infra/modules/data/tests/data.tftest.hcl:115 codifies the mistaken policy rather than exercising externally meaningful behavior.
blockers.required_fix: Apply the wrong-algorithm/key denials only when the corresponding header is present, such as with a Null condition plus StringNotEquals. Add behavioral evidence that a headerless signed PUT succeeds while wrong algorithm, wrong key, unsigned GET, and insecure transport fail.

blockers.problem: Confirmed PHI retention/data-loss risk: production current and noncurrent audio retention silently default to the synthetic seven-day values. Production enablement validates only database availability and backup retention, and the example at infra/envs/prod/foundation/terraform.tfvars.example:30 omits audio retention. Enabling that configuration would expire production audio under a policy that docs/ops/deployment-contract.md:45 explicitly records as undecided.
blockers.required_fix: Require explicit approved production values for current and noncurrent audio retention, including the legal-hold decision, before enabled=true. Update the production example and add failure tests for omitted decisions.

blockers.problem: S5 acceptance remains unverifiable: the document says no resources have been applied and records regional RDS compatibility/minor verification, applied-resource inspection, LatestRestorableTime, upload behavior, encryption metadata, and runtime-role negative checks as pending. Consequently recoverability and least-privilege behavior are not established by the offline gates.
blockers.required_fix: After fixing the policy and completing S6 roles, apply to approved synthetic staging and record the required cloud evidence: supported RDS configuration, private/encrypted resources, advancing restore time, upload positive/negative cases, object KMS metadata, queue settings, and denied runtime control mutations.

blockers.problem: The proposed batch includes hundreds of kilobytes of transient prompts, transcripts, duplicate gate logs, and prior verdicts under .agents/runs. No credential was found by the targeted scan, but committing internal orchestration history adds repository noise and unnecessary operational disclosure.
blockers.required_fix: Exclude the run directory from the commit and add an appropriate ignore rule if these artifacts are always local.
